documents.title: Refill - nose spray
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Could you send a refill of my desmopressin spray? My hematologist retired and the bottle I have expired in January. I've only used it twice this winter for nosebleeds.

documents.title: RE: Refill - nose spray
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Sent a new bottle to your pharmacy. Same as before: one spray in one nostril only for a bleed that won't stop with 10-15 minutes of pressure, and no more than one dose in a day without calling. Limit how much water you drink for the rest of that day. If you'd like a new hematologist, let us know and we'll set it up.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ANNUAL PHYSICAL

33 y/o, son is 10 months old and walking along the furniture. Working full time at the library again. Energy 'fine for a parent of a baby.' Occasional nosebleed. On HRT, no breakthrough bleeding. No new concerns.

Meds: ferrous sulfate 325 daily, ethinyl estradiol/norethindrone acetate 5 mcg/1 mg daily, vitamin D3 2000 IU, desmopressin nasal PRN.
Allergies: latex.
PMH: vWD type 1, Kallmann syndrome, iron deficiency; 2023 delivery with uterine inversion, PPH x2, D&C.
FH/SH unchanged. Never smoker, no alcohol.

ROS otherwise negative.

EXAM: Slim, well. Vitals as recorded. HEENT normal, no epistaxis. Thyroid normal. Heart RRR without murmur; lungs clear. Breasts deferred - pt declined today. Abdomen benign. Pelvic: external genitalia normal, cervix normal; Pap/HPV obtained (non-latex speculum cover and gloves). Skin: no bruising today. Mood bright, PHQ-2 0.

PLAN:
- CBC, ferritin, lipids, vitamin D.
- Pap with HPV today.
- Continue meds. Flu and COVID in the fall.
- Hematology: her doctor has retired; she'll think about a new one before any future pregnancy.

documents.title: Physical results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Maya, your Pap is normal and HPV negative, so the next one isn't due for five years. Hemoglobin 11.7 and ferritin 21 - the best they've been since you joined us. Cholesterol is good and vitamin D is 34. Keep the iron going.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Vaccines
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Late-day vaccine clinic. Flu (trivalent) L arm, 2024-25 COVID R arm. Latex-free supplies. Held pressure longer for vWD; small bandage only. Stayed 15 min without problems.

documents.title: Telehealth Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video visit from the library break room; identity confirmed.

She and her husband want a second child and she has asked the same REI group to see her again in January. Wants to know what to tell them and whether anything should change first.

Discussed: last pregnancy ended with inversion and two hemorrhages; obstetrics and REI should know that from the start, and a hematologist should be involved in delivery planning. She'll ask obstetrics to arrange one. Iron stores were at their best in May; keep iron going. She will stop HRT when REI tells her to.

No symptoms today. Continue current meds. Will send her a summary of the 2023 hospital stays through the portal so she can share it.

documents.title: Reproductive Endocrinology Return Consultation
documents.author: reproductive endocrinology
documents.body:
REPRODUCTIVE ENDOCRINOLOGY - RETURN VISIT
Date of visit: 2025-01-14

Ms. Klein, now 33, returns hoping for a second pregnancy. Kallmann syndrome; conceived in 2022 on her second gonadotropin cycle. That pregnancy ended in a vaginal birth complicated by acute uterine inversion and primary postpartum hemorrhage, then a secondary hemorrhage from retained placenta needing D&C. Type 1 von Willebrand disease; iron deficiency on oral iron. Latex allergy.

Plan:
- Gonadotropin ovulation induction as before, with monitoring here.
- Stop her estradiol/norethindrone now; first stimulation with her next scheduled start.
- Early referral to obstetrics once pregnant, with a request that hematology take part in delivery planning given the prior hemorrhages.

documents.title: Obstetrics Prenatal Update
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
OUTSIDE OBSTETRICS - LETTER TO PRIMARY CARE
Date of visit: 2025-08-19

G2P1 at about 22 weeks, conceived with ovulation induction. Anatomy ultrasound normal: appropriately grown single fetus, normal survey, placenta fundal and clear of the os.

History: her first birth (2023) was vaginal and was followed by an acute uterine inversion with primary postpartum hemorrhage needing manual replacement and transfusion, then a secondary hemorrhage from retained placenta needing D&C. Type 1 von Willebrand disease. Kallmann syndrome. Iron deficiency.

Plan after counseling: scheduled cesarean at 39 weeks given the prior inversion, with hematology input on hemostatic support. She has asked for tubal ligation at the same operation and has signed consent. Blood bank sample and crossmatch to be arranged before surgery.

events.reason: Scheduled cesarean delivery with tubal ligation

documents.title: Obstetric Discharge Summary
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
OBSTETRIC DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted: 2025-12-16  Discharged: 2025-12-19

34-year-old G2P1 at 39 weeks for scheduled cesarean (indication: prior acute uterine inversion) and bilateral tubal ligation. Type 1 von Willebrand disease - hematology recommendations followed in the OR. Kallmann syndrome. Iron deficiency. Latex allergy - latex-free room.

PROCEDURE 12/16: low transverse cesarean section under spinal anesthesia with delivery of a healthy infant, followed by bilateral tubal ligation. The case was complicated by significant hemorrhage; she was transfused 2 units of packed red cells and hemostasis was achieved.

Postoperative course: slow to mobilize because of fatigue and lightheadedness, otherwise unremarkable. Incision clean. Breastfeeding attempted with lactation support; supply low, supplementing.

DIAGNOSES: term pregnancy, delivered by cesarean; bilateral tubal ligation; postpartum hemorrhage with acute blood-loss anemia, transfused; type 1 von Willebrand disease.

DISCHARGE MEDICATIONS: ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily; vitamin D3 2000 IU daily; desmopressin nasal PRN.

FOLLOW-UP: obstetrics wound check in one week.

documents.title: Obstetrics Post-operative Visit
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
OBSTETRICS - POSTOPERATIVE VISIT
Date of visit: 2025-12-22

One week after her cesarean and tubal ligation (second child), a delivery complicated by hemorrhage requiring transfusion. She came with her husband and the baby.

She describes deep exhaustion, an inability to produce any milk though she has been putting the baby to the breast often, lightheadedness whenever she stands, and difficulty keeping her mind on things. Of note she has had no vaginal bleeding or lochia at all since the delivery.

Vitals: BP 92/56, pulse 92. Exam unremarkable other than pallor; incision healing well.
Labs today: sodium 132, glucose 64. Urine pregnancy test negative.

Assessment: postoperative check after cesarean with significant hemorrhage. Her symptoms, absent lochia, low sodium and low glucose after a second major postpartum bleed raise concern for pituitary insufficiency.
Plan: we are sending this note to her primary care physician and recommend prompt endocrinology evaluation of pituitary function. Return precautions given for vomiting, confusion or fainting.

documents.body: Obstetric discharge summary (12/16-12/19, received 12/23) and post-op visit note 12/22 (received today) filed. Post-op note flagged by OB for PCP attention - routed.

orders.reason: Suspected pituitary insufficiency after postpartum hemorrhage

documents.title: Call re: OB note
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Read the OB post-op note: Na 132, glucose 64, orthostatic symptoms, no lactation and no lochia after a second hemorrhage. Called pt: endocrinology referral placed today for a pituitary evaluation, asked for the first available. Told her to eat regularly, salt her food, and go to the ED for vomiting, confusion or fainting. She understands. She'll get the baby's checkup done this week and is home with her husband.
